LLM4Eval@SIGIR 2025 workshop invites submissions on LLM-based evaluations in IR, exploring new opportunities, limitations, and hybrid approaches. The Third Workshop on LLM4Eval at SIGIR 2025 invites submissions exploring new opportunities, limitations, and hybrid approaches involving LLM-based evaluations in Information Retrieval (IR). Recent advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have significantly impacted evaluation methodologies in IR, reshaping the way relevance, quality, and user satisfaction are assessed. Submissions are encouraged on topics including, but not limited to:. * LLMs for query-document relevance assessment. * Evaluating conversational IR and recommendation systems with LLMs. * Hybrid evaluation frameworks combining LLM and human annotations. * Identifying failure modes and limitations of LLM annotations. * Prompt engineering strategies for improving LLM annotation quality. * Paper submission deadline: April 23, 2025 (AoE). * Notification of acceptance: May 21, 2025 (AoE). * Workshop date: July 17, 2025. Mukhammadjon Musaev, Dilshod Juraev, Mannon Ochilov, Malika Abdullaeva; Text processing technology in Uzbek speech to sign language translation systems. This article analyzes methods for developing systems that translate speech into sign language. It describes the main sequence employed in these translation systems, focusing on the methods and algorithms used in speech recognition and translation modules for sign language. The sequence proposed in the article details the procedure for translating speech or text into sign sentences using natural language processing techniques. Additionally, the steps of dataset formation for the proposed translation system and the evaluation results of generating gesture video animations based on sign language grammar are presented.
